summary: Customer reported intermittent accuracy regressions and tail latency spikes after switching to an AWQ build in their on-prem Dedicated setup. This call enumerated hypotheses (layerwise quant mismatch, KV cache staleness, batching heuristics sticky to long prefixes, network jitter affecting KV transfer), reviewed perf traces they sent, and agreed a triage plan: prefix-replay stress, per-layer sensitivity sweep, KV cache TTL/eviction experiment, and on-prem profiling with perf counters.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-11 15:30 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood Infra), Laura Kim (Vantage Labs, Head ML Eng), Rafael Torres (Platform Lead), Maya Singh (ML Scientist), Tom O'Neill (SRE)

Summary (auto): Went through AWQ vs INT8/FP8 tradeoffs, dug into K-V cache sticky batch behavior on long-prefix workloads, and sketched an on-prem profiling/triage plan.

00:00:02 Alyssa (AE): Hi everyone welcome, uh Laura thanks for carving out time. Quick agenda — understand the regression, walk the traces you sent, align on hypotheses and next steps.

00:00:20 Laura (Customer): Thanks. We started seeing accuracy drift after we swapped to the AWQ build last week. It's intermittent — small hallucinations and some token shifts on longer context conversations.

00:00:35 Samir (SE): When you say "swapped" can you confirm both the quant artifact and runtime exactly? AWQ build, runtime flags, kernel versions, all that. Sometimes the compile-time quant table doesn't match the runtime dequant path.

00:00:50 Rafael (Customer): Yes we used the AWQ-1.2 artifact from your catalog and the runtime 2.7.1 that our on-prem package pulled. We did a rolling restart. GPU drivers on the node are 535.xx.

00:01:10 Samir: OK. A few quick fast hypotheses from our side: 1) per-layer scale mismatch in AWQ vs floating run causing small bias, 2) KV cache staleness + sticky batches causing degraded prefix material, 3) batching heuristics leading to head-of-line latency and opportunistic fallback firing, 4) on-prem jitter or PCIe noise corrupting hotkvs — less likely but we've seen weird edge cases.

00:01:45 Tom (SRE): We did notice spikes in tail latency around the same time as the regression windows. Our infra shows some network interface drops on the NIC (flapping small packets) coincident with heavy KV traffic.

00:02:05 Maya (Scientist): The diffs we saw are subtle — sometimes the model picks a shorter token or swaps prefere... preference from 'consistent' to 'consistently' — not huge but for our LLM benchmark (intent extraction) it reduces F1 by 3–4 points on a small prompt subset.

00:02:24 Samir: That tracks. AWQ sometimes changes the numeric distribution in higher-order moments which affects greedy decodes. Also if KV keys or values are being truncated or partially evicted because of misconfigured TTL/eviction, later layers may compensate incorrectly.

00:02:40 Laura: We also saw that if we hammer the model with long prefixes the regression is worse. Short chat replies seem fine.

00:02:55 Samir: Long prefix path heavy use of KV cache is the main suspicious area. Two sub-hypotheses: sticky batching — requests with long prefix push KV into a warm state but batching groups can interleave different prefixes causing old values to be used or KV coherence issues; or cache evictions triggered by memory pressure that happen mid-session producing slightly different generation.

00:03:20 Diego (Infra): On our on-prem Dedicated boxes we run a kernel-level shared mmap for KV to reduce copy cost. If there's a version mismatch between the compiled model kernels and runtime mmap layout, that could produce memory aliasing. We should verify ABI.

00:03:40 Rafael: Is that something AWQ would change vs GPTQ/INT8?

00:03:47 Samir: Potentially. AWQ's packing format and per-block quant scales can modify the expected memory layout. GPTQ often packs per-channel differently. FP8 is more straightforward as it's a floating-ish representation, but FP8 may cost more latency and memory.

00:04:05 Laura: Can we get a matrix from you about latency/throughput and expected accuracy delta for AWQ vs INT8 vs FP8 for our model (OpenLlama-13B variant)?

00:04:18 Alyssa: Yes we'll produce a tailored matrix and include the perf counters output we need. Samir can you add the per-layer sensitivity sweep to that?

00:04:28 Samir: Yep. Plan: run per-layer ablation where we keep higher precision on suspected sensitive layers and quantize the rest. We'll also run an AWQ->INT8 crossover to see if the regression persists.

00:04:40 Maya: Any quick wins on the runtime? We have an SLO for p95 latency 220ms and p99 480ms. The p99 spikes are what kill us.

00:04:52 Diego: If batching is too eager, head-of-line blocking can cause p99 to spike; we can tune max batch size and batch timeout, and enable KV pre-warm on session start for long-prefix flows to reduce on-demand KV transfers. But pre-warm increases memory pressure. It's tradeoff.

00:05:15 Tom: We suspected that when many sessions with long prefixes come in, the batcher groups them and the kernel picks a merge path that disables some fused kernels causing slower per-token time.

00:05:35 Samir: Right, that happens when the batch contains heterogeneous sequence lengths; runtime selects a slower codepath sometimes. Two operational mitigations: sequence-length bucketing in the batcher or sticky-routing based on prefix length to keep long-prefix sessions on a path tuned for them.

00:05:55 Laura: Are those features available in the on-prem runtime version we're on?

00:06:02 Diego: We have a bucketed batcher in 2.8.x, backports exist for 2.7.1 but need a rebuild. We can patch and test.

00:06:12 Rafael: A more immediate concern — we have strict encryption at rest and our KMS provider has a rotating key schedule. Could decryption latency/interruption tie into this?

00:06:25 Samir: If model artifacts or quant tables are lazily decrypted per request and there's a transient, yes. But Redwood's on-prem bundle supports local key caching to avoid per-request KMS hits. We should confirm your config.

00:06:40 Laura: I'll have Tom confirm key caching.

00:06:47 Alyssa: Ok let's walk the traces Rafael sent. (Alyssa shares link) Trace 1 shows a p99 spike at 14:12:43 with KV hit rate dropping to 67 percent and batch sizes rising to 48.

00:07:10 Samir: That KV hit rate dip is telling. If the cache starts missing it forces recompute or slow-path KV population which changes distribution. Also if AWQ quantization changes embedding similarity slightly, lookups that used to hit might start missing.

00:07:28 Maya: So it could be an interaction — quantization changed embeddings leading to KV misses leading to poorer context?

00:07:34 Samir: Exactly. Two-pronged experiment: a) compute embeddings pre- and post-quantization and measure L2/cosine drift on a corpus; b) run the prefix-replay stress where we replay 10k real sessions under different quant builds and capture token diffs and KV hit rates.

00:07:55 Diego: For on-prem profiling we'll enable perf counters around GPU memory copies and PCIe throughput to look for jitter. We'll also enable a network packet capture for the NIC to check for small retransmits during the windows.

00:08:10 Tom: We can do that but need guidance on low-overhead capture flags.

00:08:15 Diego: We'll use ring-buffered pcap and only pull the slices that match timestamps. Samir can provide precise time windows from the stress run.

00:08:28 Samir: I'll add instrumentation hooks in the stress runner to annotate the logs with request IDs so you can correlate network traces with token diffs.

00:08:40 Laura: Quick question on degradations — is it safe to fallback to INT8 runtime for a canary while maintaining production? We want minimal churn.

00:08:50 Samir: Yes, Redwood's runtime supports precision-gating and canary routing. We can route a small percentage of traffic to an INT8 variant with the same weights and compare outputs. If the INT8 path shows no regression, that's a clue. If it does, the issue is probably model or data side.

00:09:08 Alyssa: Let's document the exact canary plan in the next steps.

00:09:15 Maya: On the accuracy side, we also worry about stochastic rounding in mixed-precision. AWQ's default uses nearest rounding; stochastic rounding can mitigate some drift but increases variance. Has Redwood tested stochastic rounding on our model shape?

00:09:30 Samir: We have a small internal sweep for stochastic rounding. It can help in some top-k cases but may worsen deterministic evals. We'll add it to the sweep matrix.

00:09:45 Rafael: Any quick numbers — delta in throughput/latency vs FP8 vs INT8 vs AWQ? Even ballpark.

00:09:55 Samir: Ballpark on the 13B on your GPUs: FP8 ~ baseline latency, INT8 ~ 1.25x speedup token throughput, AWQ ~ 1.4x but with slightly higher variance in token probabilities. Memory footprint AWQ < INT8 < FP8 typically, but AWQ packing yields better peak memory in many cases. We'll put exact matrix in the follow-up.

00:10:20 Laura: Ok good. I want to call out a behavior: when we warm sessions with a scripted prefix the p99 drops dramatically. When sessions are cold and get a long prefix the p99 spikes. So pre-warm seems to help.

00:10:35 Samir: Pre-warm is a solid operating knob; the tradeoff is you pay memory and some extra precompute cost. We can also implement a lightweight pre-warm that only warms top-k layers or the KV index without full decoding.

00:10:50 Diego: That would be lower memory footprint and faster to run. We'll prototype a top-k-kv pre-warm.

00:10:58 Alyssa: Action items recap: Samir runs per-layer sweep and prefix-replay stress; Diego and Tom will set up on-prem perf counters and NIC captures; Laura to provide failing prompts and artifact hashes; Alyssa will share docs. We'll schedule follow-up in one week.

00:11:20 Laura: Anything else? We briefly mentioned compliance — the private deployment checklist and SSO changes we need for our auditors.

00:11:30 Alyssa: I'll include the Private deployment compliance pack and the canary runbook.

00:11:36 (small cross talk)

00:11:50 Samir: One more note on tooling — we'll produce a token-level diff report that highlights where tokens differ and attach KV hit/miss annotation per token so you can see causality. That usually helps triage quickly.

00:12:05 Rafael: Perfect.

00:12:10 Laura: Great thanks everyone.

00:12:15 Alyssa: Thanks all, we'll follow up with dates.

[End of meeting transcript excerpt — meeting continued with tactical scheduling and log links not included here due to link policy.]

1) Prefix-replay stress: Samir to run 10k session replay across AWQ/INT8/FP8, capture token diffs, KV hit rates (due 2027-08-18).
